title: Red-light places in Henderson
summary: He recalls Sally Smith's house in Audubon and its player piano.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Ah, Lee, who was in your hometown there in Henderson, weren't there? Some red light districts. I know they had, didn't they have a place called Audubon, Sally Smith Heart?
Ah, yes, it was a place there called Sally Smith Hearts. It was out in Audubon, in the East End. It was quite a notorious place and quite an exclusive place, you know.
Ah, didn't, did they have a player piano?

Yeah, they had an old player piano. You put a nickel in the, oh yeah. Then what I would get a kick out of, if you would go by there, well you would see the women with their bare legs sticking out the window shaking them all like, Ah, you boys!
Wasn't there some sort of a tradition they used to say about Sally and her best, and the best customers in the house?
Well, yes, I just don't recall just how that phrase went.
